items.text: MAP THE ZONE: Identify the car-free city center
DECODE PROS & CONS: Listen for advantages and challenges
NAVIGATE STREETS: Master directions and landmarks

strategy_items.text: Look at the map on the board (WB p. 19).
Can you find the gray area? What do you think it is?

slides.title: MAP DISCOVERY
slides.text: Look at the map in your workbook (p. 19). Find the gray area and discuss with your partner what it might be.

strategy_items.text: PREDICT: Look at the gray car-free zone. What are the advantages and disadvantages?

slides.title: ADVANTAGES & DISADVANTAGES?
slides.content:
ADVANTAGES?DISADVANTAGES?
Better air / HealthierHarder to get around
Safer for walkingInconvenient for cars
Quieter city centerProblems for some users

slides.context_sentence: It's much safer for pedestrians with no cars there.
They'll appreciate the cleaner air – there isn't nearly as much air pollution.
When he needs to go out, he can park in a handicapped parking space.
They'll appreciate the cleaner air – there isn't nearly as much air pollution.

strategy_items.text: ACTIVE LISTENING: Listen for words like 'nice', 'safe', or 'healthier' to spot advantages.
SIGNAL WORDS: Watch out for 'but', 'hard', or 'difficult'—these often signal a disadvantage.
SUMMARIZE: Don't write every word! Use short phrases (e.g., 'no cars = quiet') to fill your chart.

slides.title: THE ADVANTAGE AUDIT
slides.content:
THE VOICES

Listen to a host mother talking about the map with an exchange student.


THE MISSION

Complete the chart with the advantages and disadvantages of the car-free zone that they mention.

slides.title: THE CAR-FREE CHART
slides.content:
ADVANTAGESDISADVANTAGES
Nice for walking / SaferHard for wheelchair users
Quieter / HealthierDifficult for small kids
Cleaner air (less pollution)Transport problems

slides.question: What are the advantages mentioned?
slides.evidence: [Para 16] "And being car-free makes the area really nice for walking. It’s much safer for pedestrians... it’s a lot quieter without cars."

slides.question: What are the disadvantages mentioned?
slides.evidence: [Para 21] "Well, my uncle uses a wheelchair... he can’t go into the car-free zone... what about people with small children?"

strategy_items.text: LANDMARK FOCUS: Identify the building first (e.g., school), then find the preposition that connects it to the road.
PATH TRACKING: Use 'ALONG' for movement on a road and 'FOR' when scanning the horizon for a specific target.
DIRECTIONAL CUES: Listen for 'IN' to specify the general orientation before confirming the exact spot.

slides.title: NAVIGATION PHRASES
slides.content:
ITEMCORRECT WORD
a) According...TO the scale
b) ... the keyCHECK the key
c) go... directionIN this direction
d) go east... roadALONG this road
e) look out...FOR the supermarket
f) what... meanDOES this symbol mean
g) ... a shortcutTAKE a shortcut

strategy_items.text: CONTEXT SCAN: Look at who is speaking. Is it Rob or Kim? What are they trying to do?

slides.question: Dialogue Completion (Kim & Rob)
slides.answer: 1. d) Go east along this road
slides.evidence: [Para 5] "you go east along this road"

slides.question: Dialogue Completion (Kim & Rob)
slides.answer: 2. f) what does this symbol mean
slides.evidence: [Para 6] "And what does this symbol mean?"

slides.question: Dialogue Completion (Kim & Rob)
slides.answer: 6. e) look out for the supermarket

slides.question: Dialogue Completion (Kim & Rob)
slides.evidence: [Para 10] "Well, if you go in this direction"

strategy_items.text: Choose your destination: Theater, Beach, or Park.
Use the navigation phrases from today.
Trace the path on the map as you speak!

slides.title: CAR-FREE CITIES?
slides.content: Do you think the advantages outweigh the disadvantages? Why?
